div.p: Best wishes to you both for the New Year. I hope Sullivan sent you the passes and that you were able to go and hear him.

div.note: The face of this postcard reproduces a color illustration of a basket of flowers by “A. Vasset,” with the printed New Year’s greeting “Bonne Année.” “A. Vasset” was likely Albert Vasset, a “dessinateur” (draughtsman) who lived in Paris in the early 1900s and was a member of the Société Nationale d’Horticulture de France (Journal de la Société Nationale d’Horticulture de France, Liste Générale des Membres [Paris, 1906], 166). Vasset’s meticulous, realistic drawings of morning glories and other flowers, plants, and fruits were reproduced in Revue horticole in the 1920s.

John O’Sullivan, or Sullivan (1877-1955), Irish tenor who was a leading performer of the Paris Opéra and whom JJ was enthusiastically promoting at this time. For a fuller account, see Lucia Joyce to Pound, 22 February 1930, notes.

note.p: On 26 December 1930, John O’Sullivan sang the role of Arnold in the opera Guillaume Tell (1829) by the Italian composer Gioachino Rossini (1792-1868), at the Teatro Carlo Felice, the principal opera house of Genoa, Italy. For a more detailed account of this performance, see JJ to Pound, n.d. [mid-December 1930], notes.

An undated letter from JJ to Pound, most likely from December 1930, also mentioned O’Sullivan’s 26 December appearance in Genoa and said that JJ had asked O’Sullivan to send Pound two passes. Pound typed a note to JJ on the reverse of that letter, saying that the “tickets” hadn’t come and he was damned if he was going to the opera anyway (see JJ to Pound, n.d. [mid-December 1930], notes).
